  Terse gloss: "From outside, outwardly; denoting external origin, outer surface, or outward appearance in contrast to what is within."
  Readable gloss: "An adverb meaning 'from outside' or 'outwardly,' used to mark the external surface or origin of something as opposed to its interior. In Jesus' memorable rebuke of the Pharisees (Matt 23:25-28), the word draws a sharp contrast between outward religious polish and inner corruption — cups clean on the outside but filthy within, whitewashed tombs beautiful externally but full of dead bones. Mark 7:15, 18 similarly distinguishes what enters a person from outside versus what comes from within the heart. The multilingual evidence uniformly renders this as 'from outside' (Spanish de afuera, French au-dehors, German von aussen), confirming a single consistent spatial sense across all thirteen occurrences."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "from outside, outwardly, external"
    Enriched: Spatial adverb indicating origin from outside, the outer surface, or external appearance as contrasted with the interior. In the Synoptic Gospels it appears in Jesus' teaching on inner versus outer purity: the outside of the cup (Matt 23:25), the outside of the tomb (Matt 23:27), and what enters from outside the body (Mark 7:15, 18). Languages consistently translate with directional 'from-outside'...
    Existing Spanish translations: de-afuera, de-fuera, exterior, fuera, por-fuera
